chunks: From him, from his father, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Malik, from Muhammad ibn Nima al-Saluli, from Wahib ibn Hafas, from Abdullah ibn al-Qasim, from Abdullah ibn Khalid, from Abu al-Safatij, from Jabir ibn Yazid, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), from Jabir ibn Abdullah al-Ansari, who said:

I entered upon Fatima (peace be upon her) and a tablet was placed before her containing the names of the successors from her progeny. I counted twelve names, the last of whom was Al-Qa'im; three of them were named Muhammad and three of them were named Ali.
ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet's daughter Fatima have regarding the names of her successors?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Kitab al-Ghayba* highlights the concept of *al-Lawh* (the tablet) as a divine record of the Twelve Imams, emphasizing their specific lineage through Fatima al-Zahra. The repetition of the names Muhammad and Ali underscores the prominence of these two figures in the Imamate, while the inclusion of Al-Qa'im confirms the finality of the twelve and points to the Mahdi. This report serves as a key textual evidence for the Shia doctrine of the fixed number of Imams and their infallible succession.
